voyage.name: Ultra Music Festival
voyage.content: Streets of downtown Miami. People from around the world flock to Miami every March for its notorious Ultra Music Festival. It’s a three-day and -night festival that includes the most famous DJs in the music industry. Tickets usually range from $300–600 from the three-day festival and increase in price as it gets closer to the show in March. The show sells out almost every year so be sure to get your tickets as soon a

voyage.name: Calle Ocho
voyage.content: The largest Hispanic street festival in Miami. It’s a one-day festival that features contests, concerts and food. There is also a carnival that takes place in a lot to the left of Florida International University’s main entrance. The carnival is on the same day as Calle Ocho. The festival is usually held in March on Calle Ocho. It is free except for parking if you bring your car.

voyage.name: Carnaval Miami
voyage.content: A festival that consists of ten events along the course of ten days during the weeks of late February and early March. The Kiwanis club of little Havana (little Cuba) hosts this festival full of music, international foods, concerts, sports, culinary competitions, galas and upscale Latin jazz festival.

voyage.name: Independence Day
voyage.content: City-wide. Held on July 4. The Miami skyline is illuminated by fireworks on the “birth date” of the United States. While Key Biscayne has great views of the fireworks show, Bayfront Park has live music as well as a laser show.

voyage.name: King Mango Strut
voyage.address: Main Avenue and Grand Avenue in Coconut Grove
voyage.content: Held after Christmas, this parade began as a parody of current events as well as the Orange Bowl Parade. The Orange Bowl Parade, unlike its famous Rose Bowl counterpart, is no longer held anymore, but the King Mango Strut is still having a good time making fun of the previous year’s follies.

voyage.name: Bayfront Park
voyage.content: This park has two amphitheaters (one large and a one smaller) and hosts live performances. This park also has memorials for the astronauts who perished in the Challenger spaceship accident, former president John F. Kennedy (the JFK Torch of Friendship), and a fountain dedicated to Claude Pepper, a distinguished US congressman.

voyage.name: Miami Circle
voyage.content: An archaeological site — a 38 ft circle of holes and wood claimed to date back somewhere between 1,700 and 2,000 years old.

voyage.name: Brickell Key
voyage.content: An island community, attached to Brickell by a pedestrian friendly bridge. It is home to the famed Mandarin Oriental hotel. Strollers along Brickell Key often spot one of the many giant iguanas that make the island their home.

voyage.name: Jungle Island
voyage.content: Formerly Parrot Jungle, it's a lush tropical garden that features animal shows and exhibits. Animal encounters are available for an additional charge.

voyage.name: Miami Seaquarium
voyage.content: This 38-acre tropical island paradise features marine shows and marine life exhibits. Expect to stay around 2-3 hours touring the large aquarium. 10 minutes from downtown Miami and directly adjacent to Fairchild Tropical Botanical Garden.

voyage.name: Miami Children's Museum
voyage.content: Parking available for $2/hr.

voyage.name: Gesu Church
voyage.content: Historic Roman Catholic church, built in 1896.

voyage.name: Trinity Episcopal Cathedral
voyage.content: Built in 1925, this is the cathedral church of the Episcopal Diocese of Southeast Florida.

voyage.name: Bayside Marketplace
voyage.content: Shopping, dining, and special boat tours of surrounding islands, including the island where celebrities live.

voyage.name: Kaseya Center
voyage.content: In addition to Miami Heat (an NBA team) games being played here, this arena has hosted several awards shows in its past such as the MTV Video Music Awards (twice). Several concerts are also held here. Call box office for ticket information.

voyage.name: Simpson Park Hammock
voyage.content: Urban park and nature preserve

voyage.name: Alice Wainwright Park
voyage.content: Waterfront park and nature preserve.

voyage.name: Club Space Miami
voyage.content: Voted best U.S. club at the IDMA 2011 Awards. Known for its Saturday nights. There are multiple rooms with different genres of music in each room so you can choose from a wide variety. They hold events almost every weekend with themed parties and well known/famous DJs.

voyage.name: The Shops at Mary Brickell Village
voyage.content: upscale shops, restaurants and bars

voyage.name: Bayside Marketplace
voyage.content: Despite having several chain stores such as the Hard Rock Café, the Gap, Sketchers and Victoria’s Secret attached to it, this mall is noted for its gorgeous views of Biscayne Bay. The only downside is that traffic is bad at Bayside when Bayfront Park is having a concert nearby. Connected to public transit via Metrorail and Metromover.

voyage.name: Buchwald Jewelers
voyage.content: The third largest jewelry building in the U.S. over 100 jewelry stores under one roof.

voyage.name: Novecento
voyage.content: A very popular Argentinian-style restaurant and bar. There is a variety of casual and fine dining options.

voyage.name: Cajun Boil Brickell
voyage.content: Seafood dishes.

voyage.name: Blackbird Ordinary
voyage.content: Cocktails and culturally inspired food.

voyage.name: Rosa Sky
voyage.content: A lively rooftop lounge.

voyage.name: Hilton Miami Downtown
voyage.content: 527-room hotel.

voyage.name: InterContinental Miami
voyage.content: 5-star hotel. 641 rooms and 34 suites, offering views of the skyline and Biscayne Bay. 66,000 square feet of meeting space, including 30 meeting and conference rooms.

voyage.name: Miami Marriott Biscayne Bay
voyage.content: All of the rooms offer some sort of view of the bay with a balcony.

voyage.name: Hilton Garden Inn Miami Brickell South
voyage.content: An urban boutique hotel that features stylish accommodations and exceptional services.

voyage.name: Holiday Inn Port of Miami Downtown
Hotel AKA Brickell (formerly The Conrad)
voyage.content: It sounded better as The Conrad, but alas, things change.

voyage.name: Four Seasons Hotel Miami
voyage.content: Has a large pool deck at the seventh-floor lobby level with a view of Biscayne Bay. This hotel takes more on an arty approach to impress you, having some rare paintings and the decor to go with it. Expect everything you will from any other Four Seasons. In your expectations include that the staff will have the "Miami-tude".

voyage.name: Mandarin Oriental Hotel
voyage.content: From the Mandarin Hotel Group. This is considered the most luxurious (and expensive) of them all. The facilities are top notch and so are the staff (depending on when you go, their turnover is way higher than it should be for a luxury chain of this size and reputation). It is commonplace to find rappers and A-listers in the pool or walking through the lobby. It is also isolated on its own island (Brickell Key) which

voyage.name: Coppertone Sign
voyage.content: The original "Coppertone Sign" which has been preserved by the City of Miami. One of MiMo Boulevard's most famous landmarks.

voyage.name: New Yorker Boutique Hotel
voyage.content: An upscale boutique hotel, built inside the shell of a 1953 motel designed by Norman Giller (a famous post World War II modern architect).

voyage.name: Selina Miami Gold Dust
voyage.content: Hostel with outdoor pool and restaurant in retrofitted motor lodge building.

voyage.name: Vagabond Hotel
voyage.content: Newly renovated with 45 loft-like, spacious rooms, an Olympic style pool, Cabana bar and Googie's Diner.

voyage.name: Institute of Contemporary Art, Miami
voyage.content: This one is good if you like trying to figure out if it's you or the painting that is touched.

voyage.name: Haitian Heritage Museum
voyage.content: Founded in 2004 to commemorate Haiti’s bicentennial independence.

voyage.name: Design District Gallery Walk
voyage.content: Taking place during the second Saturday of each month, this is an evening of art, dining, cocktails and other events in the Design District.

voyage.name: Fendi Casa
voyage.content: The first U.S.-based showroom for the Italian luxury brand.

voyage.name: MC Kitchen
voyage.content: Modern Italian cuisine by Chef Dena Marino.

voyage.name: Kush
voyage.content: Gastropub with a good local beer selection.

voyage.name: Barnacle Historic State Park
voyage.price: $2 to enter the park, collected by honor system in a drop box; under age 6 enter free. More for a tour of the building
voyage.hours: Fri-Mon 9AM-5PM with tours at 10AM, 11:30AM, 1PM, 2:30PM; closed on Tuesdays, New Year´s, Thanksgiving and Christmas days. Open for groups by reservation Wed Thu
voyage.content: One of the oldest homes in Dade County, built in 1891 on the shore of Biscayne Bay. Offers a glimpse of Old Florida during The Era of the Bay. Situated on the shore of Biscayne Bay, this was the home of Ralph Middleton Munroe, one of Coconut Grove´s most charming and influential pioneers. Today, the estate is one of the last remnants of the once vast Miami Hammock, the term for the wooded area that grew around the Mi

voyage.name: Vizcaya Museum and Gardens
voyage.content: Pseudo-Italian estate built by James Deering, of the International Harvester fortune. Includes a main house filled with art and furnishings and ten acres of gardens on Biscayne Bay. $25 adults, $10 children 6-12. Admission is free for children 5 years of age or younger. Must purchase tickets online. While this is described as something of an art museum, this is much more one of those museums that just preserved a rea

voyage.name: Plymouth Congregational Church
voyage.content: Completed in 1917, this church was built by a single man using only a hatchet, a trowel, a plumb line, and a T-square. Its architectural style was modeled after the old Spanish missions of Mexico.

voyage.name: Coconut Grove Playhouse
voyage.content: A South Florida landmark that hosted live theater from 1956-2006. It is closed and awaiting restoration.

voyage.name: The Kampong
voyage.content: An 8-acre (32,000 m²) tropical garden that forms part of the National Tropical Botanical Garden.

voyage.name: CocoWalk
voyage.hours: Sun-Thu 11AM-10PM, Fri Sat 11AM-midnight (stores), restaurants and bars open until 2AM
voyage.content: Outdoor shopping center with many familiar chain stores and restaurants in nice Mediterranean-styled architecture . Completely redone and reopened in 2023.

voyage.name: Books & Books
voyage.content: Outpost of a local chain of bookstores. Also contains a cafe. They stock almost all major books on the history of Miami that are still in print.

voyage.name: Casa Xabi
voyage.content: Delicious but extremely pricey Basque restaurant.

voyage.name: Barracuda Bar and Grill
voyage.content: This throw back to the old Grove is a "come as you are" locals spot. Enjoy their nice beer selection and shoot a game of pool or play some darts. Not expensive and open late it's always a fun time.

voyage.name: Sandbar Grill
voyage.content: There are 20 televisions in this bar. The menu has seafood specialties and $0.25 wings on Mondays. Sandbar also has theme nights like the "White Trash Bash."

voyage.name: Greenstreet Cafe
voyage.content: – Serves breakfast, lunch, and dinner. A bit more upscale but has a fantastic outside seating area for cocktails.

voyage.name: Vinoteca
voyage.content: A quiet wine bar with a wildly extensive selection.

voyage.name: Mayfair Hotel & Spa
voyage.content: Blending New York influences with the tropical vibe of Miami, the iconic Mayfair Hotel & Spa - poised in hip Coconut Grove - unveils a new layer of haute with the opening of rooftop Cabana One Lounge & Pool Club and famed New York steakhouse Angelo & Maxie’s. Gaudi-inspired design and an unpretentious ambience define this historic enclave, complete with an orchid-filled, open-air atrium, Japanese soaking tubs on priv

voyage.name: The Mutiny Hotel
voyage.content: The hotel's 12-story tower sits on Sailboat Bay. The hotel's 120 one- and two-bedroom suites all have bay or city views. While this hotel's past as a bastion of the Miami criminal underworld and artistic demimonde is the stuff of legend, the vibe now is much more old white people and an empty Mexican restaurant.

voyage.name: The Ritz-Carlton
voyage.content: This luxury hotel has a charming, Italian villa-like ambience that takes its cue from nearby historic mansion, Villa Vizcaya. With abundant roses, soaring ceilings, commanding Venetian stucco columns, a grand fireplace, sleek marble floor and soaring glass wall with views onto a garden courtyard and waterfall fountain, it is a relaxing respite within one of Miami’s most noteworthy neighborhoods. Savor Italian cuisine

voyage.name: Tower Theater
voyage.content: A prominent Art Deco landmark on Calle Ocho, airing movies subtitled in Spanish.

voyage.name: Gomez Park
voyage.content: A small park at the intersection of Calle Ocho and SW 15th Ave, named in honor of Maximo Gomez, the commander of the Cuban troops during its War of Independence in the late 19th century. 15th Ave between Calle Ocho and 9th St is paved with a beautiful wavy brick pattern with images of dominoes, and there are domino motifs throughout the design of the park, which owe its influence to the large crowd of 55-year-old-and

voyage.name: Cuban Memorial Boulevard
voyage.content: The median along this boulevard is home to many statues and monuments, including an eternal flame burning in memory of the Bay of Pigs Invasion in 1961, a statue commemorating Bay of Pigs brigade member Nestor 'Tony' Izquierdo, a large relief map of Cuba with a quote by Cuban independence leader José Martí, and many others. If you look carefully at the massive ceiba tree located here, with its large, above-ground roo

voyage.name: loanDepot Park
voyage.content: One of the newer stadiums in Major League Baseball, loanDepot Park opened in April 2012 as Marlins Park at the former site of the Orange Bowl as the new home of the renamed Miami Marlins. The futuristic, retractable-roof park broke new ground in ballpark architecture; at the insistence of the team's then-owner Jeffrey Loria, it is designed to reflect the culture of 21st-century Miami. Check website or call the toll-f

voyage.name: Little Havana Food Tour
voyage.content: in Little Havana, a lively, family-friendly neighborhood, and begin a guided edible journey through one of Miami’s oldest neighborhoods. Learn about traditional, rustic Cuban cuisine by tasting your way through the must-visit street in the area — Calle Ocho.

voyage.name: La Casa de las Guayaberas
voyage.content: A store where you can find guayaberas (a Cuban shirt that has buttons but a loose fit and pleats) for men and women. Ronald Reagan came to this store himself to buy a guayabera. Shirts can be bought off the rack or custom-tailored.

voyage.name: Back In Style Vintage & Designer Clothing & Accessories
voyage.content: Back In Style is a vintage & designer clothing & accessories showroom that is open select hours, or by appointment. Please call ahead. Named one of the top 5 vintage websites in the world by Vogue Russia, over the past 10 years Back In Style has supplied clothing to celebrities, magazines, television, and couture fashion houses. Their pieces have been featured in international publications such as Vogue, Lucky Magazi

voyage.name: Versailles Restaurant and Bakery
voyage.content: A prominent gathering place and political forum for the Cuban-American community. The desserts here are delicious.

voyage.name: Azucar Ice Cream Company, LLC
voyage.content: This "only in Miami" scoop shop, creates artisanal gourmet ice creams and tropical fruit sorbets in Cuban and Latin American inspired flavors. Flavors include Guava, Mamey, Mango and Key Lime Pie ice creams. Signature Miami flavors such as Abuela Maria (vanilla, guava, cream cheese and Maria cookies) and Cuban Rum Cake (vanilla, rum cake and walnuts) are local favs.

voyage.name: Yambo Restaurant
voyage.content: Nicaraguan. Has a take-away area and a sit-down restaurant decorated in Nicaraguan style.

voyage.name: La Carreta
voyage.content: Cuban. The flagship restaurant of a small chain of Cuban restaurants (including one location at Miami International Airport). The majority of staff speak limited English but menus are available in English and Spanish. $5–22 per person, per meal.

voyage.name: Sanguich
voyage.content: An excellent Cuban sandwich shop that also has good coffee and milkshakes.

voyage.name: Los Pinareños Fruteria
voyage.content: An authentic Latin American open-air fruit market that sells fruit smoothies and coffee, but they are best known for their sugar cane juice.

voyage.name: Cubaocho
voyage.content: Extensive rum collection and art work.

voyage.name: Jefferson House
voyage.content: Built in the 1920s it is one of few "grand hotels" in Little Havana.

voyage.name: Lyric Theater
voyage.content: Built by Geder Walker, this theater was opened in 1913 and was a major African-American entertainment destination until the 1960s. Performers from Count Basie to BB King to Aretha Franklin have performed there. Do not enter, this place is gated off and it does not function as a theater any longer.

voyage.name: D.A. Dorsey House
voyage.content: Home of the first African-American millionaire in Miami. It is a private home, so don't expect to get a tour of the place.

voyage.name: Old Black Police Precinct
voyage.content: Used from 1950 to 1962, when the Precinct was finally integrated with the main police station.

voyage.name: Lagniappe
voyage.content: Restaurant and wine bar with live music.

voyage.name: Sabor a Peru
voyage.content: This place may appear to be a small hole in the wall restaurant but it is extremely well maintained and upkept and usually has a short wait for a table. They also offer take out and delivery. This venue is very popular. If you haven't tried Peruvian food before you must order the Ceviche (Fish/Seafood) and the Lomo Saltado (Beef).

voyage.name: Hampton Inn & Suites — Miami Wynwood Design District
